newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cartel office approves utilities mergers.
newsitem.headline: German cartel office approves utilities mergers.

text.p: The German Cartel Office said on Wednesday it had approved the mergers of Thyssengas with utility RWE AG, and of utilities Bayernwerk and Isarwerke, after receiving certain promises from the companies.
The office had had reservations about the mergers, which will lead to concentrations in the energy market, but said it had extracted concessions that would ensure competition.
German cartel office approves utilities mergers

Bayernwerk has been seeking to build its stake in Isarwerke GmbH to a majority, while RWE Energie AG sought to buy 50 percent of Thyssengas. The transactions will be realised by swapping RWE's stake in Isarwerke for Viag's stake in Thyssengas.
To win approval, Bayernwerk and RWE promised to honor a contract between Isarwerke and RWE unit Lechwerke AG.
The cartel authority was concerned about the Thyssengas deal because Thyssengas is supplier to gas distributors owned by RWE.
But the companies promised to improve competitive opportunities for other competitors in the affected areas, for example by building new pipelines.
